gloss: that much; to that extent; so much

definitions.gloss: that much; to that extent; so much (as was seen/experienced)
definitions.explanation: Refers back to a degree or extent that both speaker and listener are aware of, often expressing surprise, frustration, or emphasis about how much something was the case.

examples.japanese: あれほど{言|い}ったのに。
examples.english: Even though I told you so many times.

examples.japanese: あれほど{練習|れんしゅう}したのに、{本番|ほんばん}で{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: Despite practicing that much, I failed at the real performance.

examples.japanese: あれほど{注意|ちゅうい}したのに、また{同|おな}じ{間違|まちが}いをしている。
examples.english: Even though I warned you that many times, you're making the same mistake again.

notes:
Part of the こそあど demonstrative system: これほど (this much), それほど (that much, near listener), あれほど (that much, shared knowledge). あれほど refers to a degree that both speaker and listener have witnessed or experienced.

USAGE:
Very commonly followed by のに (despite) to express frustration or exasperation. The pattern あれほど〜のに conveys 'even though (it was that much / I did it that many times)...'

COMMON PATTERNS:
- あれほど{言|い}ったのに: I told you so many times and yet...
- あれほど{注意|ちゅうい}したのに: despite warning you so much...
- あれほどの{努力|どりょく}: that much effort

SIMILAR WORDS:
- それほど: to that extent — refers to something closer to the listener or just mentioned; often used in negative sentences (それほどでもない, not that much)
- これほど: this much — refers to the current situation or something close to the speaker
- あんなに: that much — more colloquial; similar meaning but slightly less formal
